task: v2 extension architecture design — execution-based behavioral evidence
design_principles: v1 files are FROZEN — zero modifications to sbg/, baselines/b01-b08, experiments/phase4/
v2 code lives in sbg/v2/ and experiments/v2/ exclusively
v2 modules import v1 symbols; v1 modules never import v2
b06_dynamic.py (flat trace, unstructured) is superseded by b07_dynamic_v2.py
sbg/extraction/dynamic/tracer.py is v1-frozen; v2/execution/tracer.py extends via composition

execution/.runner.py: safe sandbox execution with configurable timeout and resource caps
execution/.tracer.py: rich execution trace capture — stdout, state snapshots, exception chains, coverage
execution/.normalizer.py: strip machine-specific artefacts from raw traces before comparison
execution/.genome.py: DynamicGenome dataclass — structured summary of execution evidence

hybrid/.fusion.py: combine v1 StaticGenome dict + v2 DynamicGenome into HybridGenome
hybrid/.distance.py: weighted behavioral distance over hybrid genome; extends sbg.distance

experiments/v2/.e1_dynamic_only.py: E1: DynamicGenome alone vs v1 EXECUTION dim — coverage + output parity
experiments/v2/.e2_input_sensitivity.py: E2: how many distinct inputs are needed for stable DynamicGenome?
experiments/v2/.e3_output_equivalence.py: E3: output-vector equivalence as a standalone signal
experiments/v2/.e4_exception_behavior.py: E4: exception-pattern distance across mutation families
experiments/v2/.e5_coverage_delta.py: E5: coverage Jaccard improvement over v1 execution genome
experiments/v2/.e6_hybrid_vs_static.py: E6: HybridGenome vs static-only (B07) — same test split
experiments/v2/.e7_hybrid_vs_full_sbg.py: E7: HybridGenome vs B08 full SBG — does v2 dynamic beat v1 dynamic?
experiments/v2/.e8_safe_corpus_analysis.py: E8: executability audit — which programs yield stable traces?
experiments/v2/.e9_normalization_impact.py: E9: normalized vs raw traces — stability across runs and machines
experiments/v2/.e10_input_set_ablation.py: E10: ablation over canonical input sets (integers/lists/strings/structs)
experiments/v2/.e13_weight_search.py: E13: grid search over hybrid weights (frozen after dev; not tuned on test)
experiments/v2/.e14_regression.py: E14: full regression — all prior phase4 hypotheses re-evaluated with v2
experiments/v2/.run_all_experiments.py: sequential runner with per-experiment timeout and artifact saving

baselines/v2/.b07_dynamic_v2.py: B7v2: structured DynamicGenome baseline (replaces flat b06_dynamic.py)
baselines/v2/.b08_hybrid_sbg_v2.py: B8v2: full hybrid (v1 static + v2 dynamic) — the primary v2 claim

docs/v2/.HYPOTHESES_V2.md: new hypotheses introduced by execution-based evidence
docs/v2/.THREATS_V2.md: additional validity threats from sandbox execution

module_designs.purpose: Execute arbitrary Python source strings safely with hard resource limits
module_designs.rationale_over_v1: b06_dynamic._load_fn() uses bare exec() with no isolation; v1 Tracer requires a Callable — runner bridges source→Callable with safety guarantees

inputs.inputs: List[Any] — values to pass to the entry-point function

key_methods.run(source_code, inputs, **kwargs) -> Li: public API — load module, discover entry point, execute each input
key_methods._load_entry_point(source_code) -> Callab: exec source into isolated module, find first of main/solve/run/compute or only top-level function
key_methods._run_one(fn, inp, timeout_s) -> RunResul: delegates to v1 Tracer._trace_one() for threading+timeout; converts ExecutionTrace → RunResult

module_designs.connection_to_v1: Calls v1 Tracer._trace_one() under the hood for thread safety and timeout; reuses _TIMEOUT_SECONDS constant pattern
module_designs.entry_point_discovery: Same priority as b08_full_sbg._load_fn_from_source: main > solve > run > compute > single top-level FunctionType
what_needs_testing: timeout fires correctly for infinite-loop programs
stdout is captured and capped
load errors return exit_code=3 and non-crashing RunResult
all 64 base programs load without ImportError (stdlib-only imports)
programs with required positional args that cannot be called with test inputs return exception RunResult gracefully

module_designs.purpose: Richer execution trace capture than v1 — adds output vectors, exception chains, and per-input state snapshots
module_designs.rationale_over_v1: v1 ExecutionGenome aggregates across all inputs before storing; v2 keeps per-input records to enable output-vector comparison

RawDynamicTrace_fields.stdout_corpus: List[str] — all non-empty stdout lines across inputs

module_designs.connection_to_v1: Imports ExecutionTrace from sbg.extraction.dynamic.tracer (read-only); does NOT re-run sys.settrace — that is left to v1 Tracer
what_needs_testing: exception_rate computed correctly from mix of ok/error RunResults
stdout_lines correctly splits multi-line output
empty input list produces empty RawDynamicTrace with n_inputs=0

module_designs.purpose: Remove machine-specific, run-specific, and address-space-specific artefacts from traces before comparison
module_designs.rationale_over_v1: v1 ExecutionGenome stores repr() of local variables which contains memory addresses (e.g. <object at 0x...>); v2 must strip these for stability
normalization_rules: Replace object ids in reprs: '<ClassName object at 0xADDR>' → '<ClassName object>'
Normalize floating point noise: round floats in stdout to 6 sig figs
Strip trailing whitespace and normalize newlines in stdout_lines
Normalize file paths in exception messages: replace cwd-relative and abs paths with '<path>'
Deduplicate identical consecutive stdout lines (idempotent output reduction)
Cap stdout_lines at 500 lines per input (truncation marker added)

key_methods.normalize(raw_trace) -> RawDynamicTrace: apply all rules, return new RawDynamicTrace
key_methods._normalize_repr(s) -> str: apply address/id replacement to a single repr string

module_designs.connection_to_v1: No v1 imports needed — operates on v2 RawDynamicTrace only
what_needs_testing: Memory address regex replaces correctly and does not corrupt hex literals
Float normalization does not alter non-float strings
Path normalization handles both Unix and Windows separators
normalize(normalize(t)) == normalize(t) (idempotent)

module_designs.purpose: DynamicGenome dataclass — structured behavioral summary extracted from normalized traces
module_designs.rationale_over_v1: v1 ExecutionGenome (g_U, Definition 16) captures coverage+call-counts only; v2 DynamicGenome adds output-vector, exception fingerprint, and return-type profile

fields.n_inputs: int — number of test inputs used
fields.return_type_profile: Dict[str, float] — normalized distribution of return types
fields.output_vector_hash: str — SHA-256[:16] of sorted normalized stdout lines
fields.output_line_count_stats: Dict[str,float] — {mean,std,min,max} of per-input stdout line counts
fields.stdout_vocabulary_size: int — unique non-empty normalized output lines
fields.v1_execution_genome: Optional[ExecutionGenome] — v1 genome if tracing was available, else None
fields.provenance: Dict[str,Any] — program_id, n_inputs, input_types, extraction_timestamp, normalizer_version

module_designs.extractor_method: extract(normalized_trace: RawDynamicTrace, v1_genome: Optional[ExecutionGenome] = None) -> DynamicGenome
module_designs.connection_to_v1: Accepts an optional v1 ExecutionGenome to embed as v1_execution_genome field; v1 Tracer must be called separately by the caller
what_needs_testing: Empty trace yields DynamicGenome with all-zero/empty fields
output_vector_hash is stable across two identical runs of the same program
return_type_profile values sum to 1.0 when n_inputs > 0
v1_execution_genome field round-trips through serialization

module_designs.purpose: Combine a v1 static genome dict with a v2 DynamicGenome into a unified HybridGenome

fields.static_genomes: Dict[str,Any] — v1 dimensions keyed by CONTROL/DATA/ERROR

module_designs.function: fuse(static: Dict[str,Any], dynamic_v2: DynamicGenome, v1_dynamic: Dict[str,Any] = None) -> HybridGenome
design_notes: fuse() is a pure function — no side effects
Missing dimensions are tolerated; fusion records which are present in HybridGenome.available_dims
v1_dynamic may be None when programs are execution-unsafe (static-only fallback)
module_designs.connection_to_v1: Imports ControlGenomeExtractor, DataGenomeExtractor, ErrorGenomeExtractor from sbg.extraction.static (read-only)
what_needs_testing: fuse with all-None v1_dynamic produces HybridGenome with v1_dynamic_genomes={}
available_dims correctly reflects which fields are non-None
round-trip: fuse result can be passed directly to hybrid_distance

module_designs.purpose: Compute hybrid behavioral distance D_hybrid(H1, H2) ∈ [0,1] over HybridGenome pairs
module_designs.function: hybrid_distance(h1: HybridGenome, h2: HybridGenome, weights: Dict[str,float] = DEFAULT_V2_WEIGHTS) -> Dict[str,Any]
module_designs.note_on_weights: Sum = 1.00. DYN_ prefix = v2-only components. EXECUTION_V1 = v1 g_U distance if available, else 0-weight fallback. Weights are RE-NORMALISED over present dimensions exactly as in sbg.distance.behavioral_distance.

distance_components.DYN_RETURN_TYPE: L1 distance between return_type_profile dicts, scaled to [0,1]
distance_components.DYN_OUTPUT_VECTOR: 0.0 if output_vector_hash equal, else 1.0 (binary; add Jaccard on vocabulary as secondary)

module_designs.connection_to_v1: All v1 distance functions imported read-only; hybrid_distance wraps sbg.distance.behavioral_distance for the static+v1-dynamic slice
what_needs_testing: hybrid_distance(h, h) == 0.0 for any h
hybrid_distance(h1, h2) == hybrid_distance(h2, h1)
total_distance ∈ [0,1] under all combinations of missing dimensions
DYN_OUTPUT_VECTOR component = 0.0 when both output_vector_hash are identical

module_designs.purpose: B7v2 — improved dynamic baseline using DynamicGenome instead of flat trace features
module_designs.distance_used: DYN_EXCEPTION_RATE + DYN_RETURN_TYPE + DYN_OUTPUT_VECTOR (equal weights); pure v2 dynamic, no static features
module_designs.connection_to_v1: Uses SandboxRunner (v2) for execution; does NOT import b06_dynamic or v1 Tracer directly
what_needs_testing: Produces scores in [0,1]
Caching: same source string returns same score without re-execution
Execution-unsafe programs (those that return load_error) fall back to score 0.5 (neutral)

module_designs.purpose: B8v2 — primary v2 claim: hybrid (v1 static + v2 dynamic) SBG with DEFAULT_V2_WEIGHTS
pipeline: 1. Extract v1 static genomes (CONTROL, DATA, ERROR) via v1 extractors
4. If program is in safe corpus: also run v1 Tracer for EXECUTION/STATE/RESOURCE/TEMPORAL/INTERACTION
module_designs.connection_to_v1: Imports all v1 static extractors and v1 Tracer (composition, not modification)
what_needs_testing: End-to-end pipeline on at least 10 safe programs produces well-formed scores
Execution-unsafe programs still produce a score (static fallback)
scores match b08_full_sbg.py on execution-safe programs within expected tolerance

execution_safe_programs.safety_reason: Pure computation, stdlib only, deterministic, no I/O
In-memory sort; non-determinism only if random pivot — check implementation
State machine with deterministic tick clock, no real time
Simulated backoff on deterministic tick clock, no real sleep
In-memory INI parser, string in → dict out
In-process pub/sub, no real network, no real I/O, deterministic tick
Mock HTTP — no real sockets, no real sleep, fully in-memory
Deterministic integer-tick clock, no real time.sleep
In-memory mock REST store, no network
In-memory TTL cache with deterministic clock
Pure simulation of memory allocation, fully deterministic
In-memory scheduler with tick clock, no real threads
In-memory base64/hex encoding — no file I/O despite 'file_' prefix
Parses INI string in memory — no filesystem access
In-memory CSV processing via csv.reader(io.StringIO(...)) — no real file I/O
Parses log lines as list of strings — no filesystem access
Streaming over list of strings — no real I/O

execution_unsafe_programs.reason: Uses threading.Thread + queue — non-deterministic scheduling makes traces unstable across runs; output ordering not reproducible
execution_unsafe_programs.mitigation: Can be run but DynamicGenome components must use exception_rate + return_type_profile only; skip output_vector_hash comparison

execution_unsafe_programs.reason: Uses threading.Condition + RLock — concurrent reads/writes produce non-deterministic interleaving; trace event ordering unstable
execution_unsafe_programs.mitigation: Static-only analysis recommended; dynamic execution may be attempted with single-threaded synthetic inputs only

execution_unsafe_programs.reason: threading.RLock — non-deterministic scheduling in multi-threaded tests; however the counter itself can be exercised single-threaded safely
execution_unsafe_programs.mitigation: Use single-threaded synthetic inputs (increment/decrement calls) to exercise the counter logic deterministically

execution_unsafe_programs.reason: Likely uses threading or time.time() for real-time connection management — requires inspection
execution_unsafe_programs.mitigation: Audit for time.time() and threading before classification; may be reclassifiable as safe if tick-based

SandboxRunner.run.signature: run(source_code: str, inputs: List[Any], timeout_s: float = 5.0) -> List[RunResult]
SandboxRunner.run.contract: Never raises; wraps all errors into RunResult.exit_code. Returns len(inputs) results.

DynamicGenomeExtractor.extract.signature: extract(normalized_trace: RawDynamicTrace, v1_genome: Optional[ExecutionGenome] = None) -> DynamicGenome
DynamicGenomeExtractor.extract.contract: Deterministic for identical normalized_trace. v1_genome embedded verbatim.

fuse.signature: fuse(static: Dict[str, Any], dynamic_v2: DynamicGenome, v1_dynamic: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> HybridGenome
fuse.contract: Pure function, no side effects. Missing dimensions tolerated.

hybrid_distance.signature: hybrid_distance(h1: HybridGenome, h2: HybridGenome, weights: Dict[str,float] = DEFAULT_V2_WEIGHTS) -> Dict[str, Any]
hybrid_distance.contract: Returns dict with total_distance ∈ [0,1], symmetric, hybrid_distance(h,h)==0.0

score_fn (baselines).contract: Returns similarity ∈ [0,1] where 1.0=identical, 0.0=maximally different. Matches v1 baseline interface for drop-in comparison.

canonical_input_set_v2.name: CANONICAL_INPUTS_V2
canonical_input_set_v2.rationale: Extended from v1 b08 fixed inputs to include structured objects that exercise more code paths in OOP programs

integration_points_with_v1.integration_type: composition — SandboxRunner._run_one delegates to Tracer._trace_one for thread+timeout logic
embedding — DynamicGenome.v1_execution_genome holds an optional v1 ExecutionGenome instance
delegation — hybrid_distance calls sbg.distance.behavioral_distance for the static+v1-dynamic slice, then adds v2 components
composition — fusion.py calls v1 extractors for the static slice; does not modify them
re-use — v2 baselines use the same evaluation harness as v1 baselines for apples-to-apples comparison
reference — e14 imports phase4 results from artifacts/ and re-evaluates all H1-H12 hypotheses with v2 evidence added

criteria_for_safe: No real network I/O (socket, urllib, requests, http.client)
No filesystem writes (open(..., 'w'), pathlib.write_text, os.mkdir, etc.)
No real-time dependencies (time.sleep, time.time as clock, datetime.now)
No non-deterministic multi-threading in the program's entry-point logic
All imports resolvable from Python stdlib
criteria_for_conditional: Uses threading but entry-point is callable single-threaded (e.g. ThreadSafeCounter.increment)
Uses time.time but only as a monotonic surrogate for integer ticks
programs_inspected: fsm_traffic_light — SAFE (tick-based FSM, no real time)

v2_input_harness_design.problem: Most base programs are classes or multi-function modules, not single callables. v1 b06/b08 used _load_fn() which only found a single top-level function.
v2_input_harness_design.v2_solution: ProgramHarness — one per program_id, specifies how to instantiate and call the program

harness_schema.entry_class: str | null — class name to instantiate
harness_schema.method_sequence: List[{'method': str, 'args': List[Any]}] — sequence of method calls to make observable
harness_schema.test_fn: str | null — name of test function to call (for module_test_fn harness type)

examples.note: fib is a top-level function; SandboxRunner uses canonical integer inputs directly
Call the built-in test function — it exercises the full state machine

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Output non-determinism in programs using dict iteration order or set ordering
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: TraceNormalizer sorts output lines before hashing for output_vector_hash; raw stdout is preserved separately

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Programs with large inputs exceeding timeout on slow CI machines
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: CANONICAL_INPUTS_V2 uses small inputs only; max_total_timeout_s=30s per program

risks_and_mitigations.risk: v2 DynamicGenome is richer but harder to compare — distance may not be in [0,1]
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: All distance components are individually constrained to [0,1] before weighting; hybrid_distance clamps final result

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Weight contamination — DEFAULT_V2_WEIGHTS might be implicitly tuned on test set
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: All weight choices in DEFAULT_V2_WEIGHTS must be frozen after dev set evaluation; e13 weight search uses dev only

risks_and_mitigations.risk: conc_* programs yield different traces on different machines due to scheduler
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: conc_* programs are classified UNSAFE and excluded from output_vector_hash comparison; static-only fallback applied
